name: markdown
comment: Lightweight Markdown grammar for syntax-highlighting `:md` blocks shown inside NMBL code samples (the NMBL grammar embeds Markdown by including scope `text.html.markdown`). Why this exists and why it's shaped this way: in the website's Shiki, the Vue grammar pulls in Shiki's FULL markdown grammar as an embedded lang. That grammar (a) references `text.html.derivative` — the scope Vue uses for template bodies — and breaks the nmbl-in-vue injection, and (b) treats NMBL's indented `:md` body as an indented code block, so headings/lists render flat. We avoid loading it by registering THIS grammar under the same lang name (`markdown`) and scope (`text.html.markdown`); expressive-code loads its configured langs first, so when the Vue grammar later tries to pull in `markdown`, Shiki sees the name is already loaded and skips it — leaving this grammar in charge of the scope. Patterns tolerate leading whitespace because NMBL indents `:md` bodies. Note: this also becomes the highlighter for any ```md / ```markdown fences on the site (lightweight, which is fine here). Never touches real `:md` rendering, which goes through the markdown processor, not Shiki.
